ai.title: SDK auto-discovers project files via gitignore
ai.summary: CodebuffClient now automatically discovers project files when projectFiles is undefined, using .gitignore patterns to filter content. This change modifies sdk/src/run-state.ts to integrate getProjectFileTree and getAllFilePaths, ensuring knowledge files are derived correctly without manual configuration. The update adds the 'ignore' dependency and includes new test suites for tree-sitter queries and SDK functionality in sdk/package.json and sdk/test.

eli5.text: When you use the assistant without manually telling it which files to look at, it can now automatically find and read your project files on its own. It does this by scanning your project folder and skipping anything listed in your.gitignore file, so only relevant files get pulled in. You don't need to configure anything, if you don't specify files, this auto-discovery kicks in by default. The change is live today as part of the SDK.

ai.title: base-max overhaul with implementation-planner-max
ai.summary: base-max agent switches model to anthropic/claude-sonnet-4 and gains spawnableAgents including implementation-planner-max. New implementation-planner-max agent spawns 3 parallel implementation-planner agents then delegates selection to plan-selector. base-prompts adds isMax flag forcing implementation-planner-max spawn for medium/hard tasks. Scope covers .agents/base-max.ts, new .agents/implementation-planner/* files, and .agents/prompts/base-prompts.ts.

eli5.text: The main assistant that handles complex tasks like coding and research has been upgraded. Previously it used one specific AI model, but now it uses a more capable one, and it can bring in other specialized assistants to help it (like ones that research code, think through problems, or review work). If you give it a medium-to-hard task, it will now automatically create three different plans in parallel, compare them, and pick the best one before presenting its final answer to you. This should make the overall result higher quality since it's actively comparing multiple approaches, though the process might take a little longer as it runs through that comparison step.

Added fs.readFileSync check for absolute paths before Query instantiation. Updated evals/git-evals/runners/codebuff.ts to assign this.runState immediately from client.run, removing redundant null check.

eli5.text: The tool that reads your code now correctly handles a quirk where, under Bun, a query was given as a file path instead of the query text itself: it checks whether the path is absolute and reads the file content before using it. While testing this, the runner assigns its progress state immediately after starting rather than waiting to see if the run failed first. This affects the code-mapping and evaluation tooling and is live today.

ai.title: Fix SDK sessionState override in CodebuffClient options
ai.summary: CodebuffClient constructor no longer pre-fills default options (cwd, maxAgentSteps, etc.) into this.options, preventing overrides of sessionState in run(). Type for options changed from Required<CodebuffClientOptions> to CodebuffClientOptions with explicit apiKey/fingerprintId. run() now applies defaults (process.cwd(), MAX_AGENT_STEPS_DEFAULT) and guards optional callbacks (handleEvent, handleStreamChunk) and objects (overrideTools, customToolDefinitions) with nullish coalescing. Affects sdk/src/client.ts and sdk/src/run.ts.

eli5.text: When you create the assistant tool, it no longer fills in default settings (like the working folder or step limits) upfront, so your own settings, especially saved session state, actually take effect when the assistant runs. If you looked, you'd see the tool now waits to add those defaults only when the run starts, and it safely handles missing optional settings like event callbacks and tool lists without crashing. This is live today for anyone building with the software development kit.

ai.title: Implementation Planner Max parallel count raised to 10
ai.summary: Implementation Planner Max spawns 10 parallel agents instead of 3. Plan Selector criteria shift to Completeness, Simplicity, Quality, Efficiency, Maintainability, Risk. Reasoning effort raised to medium. Files: .agents/implementation-planner/implementation-planner-max.ts, plan-selector.ts.

eli5.text: When you ask the planning assistant to work out an implementation plan, it now drafts ten separate plans at the same time (instead of three) and then picks the best one, and the helper that chooses that best plan is now instructed to think a bit harder and judge plans by broader qualities like completeness and simplicity rather than just feasibility. These are internal settings for the assistant's own planning process, so nothing about your finished report or code changes looks different to you, but on the backend the assistant is gathering more options and weighing them more thoroughly before settling on a single plan.

ai.title: Update recommended models in agent-definition.ts
ai.summary: Updated the `ModelName` union type in `common/src/templates/initial-agents-dir/types/agent-definition.ts` to reflect current model availability. Added Gemini 2.5 flash/flash-lite preview variants, Grok 4 fast free tier, and several Qwen3 models including max, coder-plus, and coder-flash. Normalized Anthropic Claude 4 Sonnet identifier from dated suffix to `anthropic/claude-sonnet-4`. This ensures the initial agents directory template and type definitions match the active model catalog.

eli5.text: When you set up a new assistant project, the list of AI models the project is initially pointed at has been refreshed to match what is currently available. Models that were given dated labels have been cleaned up to use simpler names, and new preview versions of the Gemini 2.5 Flash models, a free tier of Grok 4 Fast, and additional Qwen3 models including coder-plus and coder-flash variants have been added. If you generate a new project from the standard template today, those newer or renamed options are offered in the starter configuration instead of the older entries they replace. This is live now for any new project you create from the template; existing projects are not affected.

ai.title: Update agent builder prompt and examples
ai.summary: Refactored `agent-builder.ts` to dynamically load high-quality example agents (researcher, implementation-planner) into the system prompt. Updated instructions to prioritize agent composition, reuse of published store agents, and simplified input/output schemas. Removed static environment setup boilerplate in favor of direct project context awareness.

eli5.text: The assistant that helps build new AI agents now gets real, working examples included right in its instructions, instead of just abstract notes about how agents should be structured. If you watched it create an agent, you'd see it reference specific, proven agent designs (like a researcher and a planning agent) as starting points, and it's now told to build groups of agents that work together rather than single, all-purpose ones. These examples are pulled in automatically from existing high-quality agent files, so updates to those templates flow through to the builder without extra effort.

ai.title: Disable commander help option in release binary
ai.summary: Added `.helpOption(false)` to the `Command` instance in `npm-app/release/index.js`. This disables the built-in `--help` flag handling by Commander, redirecting help requests to the underlying binary as noted in the analysis. The change applies to the `codebuff` CLI entry point.

eli5.text: When you run the main program and type the help command, the program now sends that request directly to the underlying tool instead of handling it itself. This only affects the release version of the program that most users run. If you look at the program's settings, you'd find one extra line that turns off the program's own help feature.

ai.title: Release 1.0.497 version bump
ai.summary: Bumped the `codebuff` package version from 1.0.496 to 1.0.497 in `npm-app/release/package.json` as part of the scheduled release pipeline. The bump follows a same-day commit sequence that introduced MCP server support in agent definitions, SDK project file auto-discovery via `.gitignore`, and the `base-max` overhaul with `implementation-planner-max` agent spawn support. Version 1.0.498 follows shortly after, indicating these features are part of an active release cadence.
ai.evidence: Commit [4862f337] modifies `npm-app/release/package.json`, incrementing the `version` field from `1.0.496` to `1.0.497`. This is a release-bump commit with +1/-1 line changes, no source code or feature modifications.

eli5.text: This release adds support for connecting external tools and servers to agents through a new Model Context Protocol (MCP) system, allowing agents to dynamically pull in capabilities from other software. It also introduces a smarter planning agent that spawns multiple parallel assistants to tackle complex coding tasks, then picks the best approach. The base agent now uses Anthropic's Claude 4 Sonnet model and can break down difficult problems into coordinated sub-tasks. Developers using the SDK will now have their project files automatically discovered without manual setup, and the list of recommended AI models has been refreshed with new options from Google, xAI, and Anthropic. Upgrading gives you more powerful autonomous coding help, better tool integration, and an improved experience when setting up projects with the SDK.

ai.title: Fix typo in release CLI helpOption call
ai.summary: Corrects `.helpOoption(false)` to `.helpOption(false)` in `npm-app/release/index.js`. The typo caused the release CLI to ignore the disable-help flag, potentially exposing unwanted help text or throwing errors during execution.

eli5.text: The assistant's release-helper tool had a small typo in one command that was supposed to turn off its help message, but it wasn't working because of the misspelled word. As a result, you might have seen extra help text appear during a release run, or in rare cases, the helper could have errored out when it thought it was still allowed to print that text. Developers noticed that the disable option was simply being ignored, so this change corrects the typo and makes the helper behave as intended when that flag is set.

ai.title: Version bump to 1.0.498
ai.summary: Bumps the `codebuff` package version in `npm-app/release/package.json` from 1.0.497 to 1.0.498 as part of the routine release sequence. This release includes a minor fix that corrects the typo `.helpOoption(false)` to `.helpOption(false)` in the release CLI, ensuring the disable-help flag is respected. The change is internal and does not alter user-facing behavior beyond the corrected CLI help option handling.
ai.evidence: Commit `6d2adb17` modifies `npm-app/release/package.json`, incrementing the version field from `1.0.497` to `1.0.498`.

eli5.text: This release fixes a small issue with the command used to create and manage new software releases. It corrects a typo that was preventing a flag from properly turning off help text when needed, which could have caused confusing output or errors during the release process. Users running release commands will see cleaner, more predictable behavior without unwanted help messages appearing. The update ensures the release tooling works exactly as intended when you or your team ship new versions.

ai.title: MCP remote servers support custom headers
ai.summary: Added `headers` field to `mcpConfigRemoteSchema` and `mcpConfigStdioSchema` in `types/mcp.ts` and `util-types.ts`. `getMCPClient` in `common/src/mcp/client.ts` now passes these headers to `StreamableHTTPClientTransport` and `SSEClientTransport` via `requestInit`. Enables authenticated access to remote MCP endpoints.

eli5.text: If you configure a remote tool server using an address and a secret token, you can now include that token (or other custom identifiers) directly in the connection setup. The system now accepts a new optional field for custom headers alongside the URL and passes those headers to the remote server when connecting. You would notice this when editing your configuration file or tool settings: a new optional section appears where you can enter header name-value pairs, and the connection to password-protected or authenticated servers succeeds where it previously could not.
